findings: BLOCKING (privacy/authority): campaign_lifecycle record-result execs exp/validate_return.py with the private checkpoint/console paths and lets exp/publication.json govern which returned bytes are copied into git, but neither file is hash-bound by verify_decision or any receipt; a post-review commit can replace either and pass all clean-tree/staleness checks. Nothing binds the returned bundle to the verified run.py either, so the whole return-import identity rests on the unbound validator. Bind validate_return.py and publication.json (and ideally requirements.txt/synthetic tests) into the receipt chain.

BLOCKING (authority): run_isolated_stage pops SCOUT_CI from the environment before run_agent, making the r.get('ci') refusal in campaign_pipeline.execute and interpret-build unreachable via that marker — CI runs are laundered as interactive instead of refused. Fail closed (raise) when SCOUT_CI is set rather than stripping it.

BLOCKING (identity binding): interpretation_receipt.json records proposal_sha256 for investigator_next_decision.json, but neither campaign_lifecycle.context() nor campaign_pipeline.grounding() verifies it, so the predecessor proposal motivating a follow-up can be altered post-review undetected. grounding() also omits the prior spec_sha256 check that context() performs.

MEDIUM (recovery/identity): job_store.Store.register does its binding-conflict read-then-INSERT OR IGNORE outside BEGIN IMMEDIATE (unlike claim/complete_event); concurrent registrations with different bindings can both appear to succeed, silently swallowing the identity conflict instead of raising.
MINOR: campaign_pipeline.grounding reads import_receipt.json via exists()/read_text() with no symlink check, inconsistent with the symlink refusal on all other bound inputs.
MINOR: the pipeline approval receipt hashes only top-level files of the approved round directory (directory.iterdir()), leaving any subdirectory artifacts unbound.
MINOR: run_isolated_stage mkdtemp roots (prompts, console logs, git repo) are never cleaned up despite the 'disposable' design; aggregate-only by policy but they persist in /tmp.

POSITIVE: job_store lease/dedup/dispatch-ambiguity semantics are correct and fail-closed (dispatch never auto-retried, stale-lease completions rejected, patient+VALIDATED routes to the human transfer inbox) and are well covered by tests; all statuses and receipts consistently avoid claiming human ratification; commit() scope guard and stage isolation (fresh temp roots, declared-output copying) prevent cross-scope writes and reviewer-artifact planting.
